questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was drawn to Canada primarily for its beautiful and unique nature, which I had always wanted to explore, and the fact that it is an English-speaking country. UBC also has a strong reputation globally, especially in law. I was interested in experiencing a different legal system and academic environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My semester at UBC was incredibly enriching. I made international friends, gained insight into Canadian law, and had the opportunity to explore breathtaking nature - from coastal hikes to snowy mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UBC provided comprehensive online resources beforehand and detailed orientation sessions upon arrival. The Go Global office was responsive and helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received an orientation package, attended welcome events, and participated in guided tours. Student volunteers and the Go Global office were available for questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation made it very easy to settle in and meet other exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed in Walter Gage Residence. It was well-located and had a great student atmosphere. However, rent was relatively expensive compared to Denmark, and the units were quite old/outdated.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a kitchen i shared with my flatmates. It was very small, and quickly got messy/dirty, so I didnt use it as much.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to buy all your own kitchen appliances and utensils. Most on-campus housing options at UBC, including places like Walter Gage do not come equipped with kitchen essentials. This means you’ll need to purchase everything from pots and pans to cutlery, plates, and even items like a kettle or toaster if you want them. Many students buy inexpensive items at nearby stores like Canadian Tire or Walmart, or second-hand through Facebook Marketplace. It’s also common to share with roommates, so coordinating can help reduce costs.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was done online through the UBC Student Service Centre. Exchange students were given specific registration dates. It required some planning, as law courses were in high demand. It was easy to self-register online, and I even switched courses in the initial 2-week period without any problems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Academic advisors and the Go Global office offered assistance via email and drop-in sessions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the courses I aimed for, but had to be flexible with one or two options.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have several backup courses ready and register as early as possible. Sign up for the waitlist if you are really interested in a course that has filled up, as people drop courses within the first 2 weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses were well-structured and professors were approachable. The academic environment encouraged critical thinking and participation.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA courses were more intensive, with higher expectations for independent work. The courses (naturally) focused a lot on Canadian law, but since the Canadian justice system is built different than was we have in Denmark, it was at times difficult to follow the lectures/syllabus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UBC had smaller classes and more frequent assessments like quizzes, midterms, and group work. There was more emphasis on in-class participation and practical examples.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAW_V 322 (3.0) International Law Problems 
LAW_V 393D (3.0) Green Rights and Warrior Lawyers 
LAW_V 410 (3.0) International Taxation
LAW_V 461 (3.0) Corporate Transactions

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Focus on courses with an international perspective, as chances are this will be most relevant for your future studies. I learned a lot in LAW_V 461 Corporate Transactions and LOVED our professor in LAW_V 410 International Taxation even though the class was very difficult academically.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some course materials weren’t available online and had to be purchased. Outdoor gear (e.g., hiking boots, rain jacket) also added up.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than expected, especially in Vancouver. Public transport was cheaper with the U-Pass.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide range of clubs, from hiking groups to debate societies. UBC Recreation offered great gym and class options.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the UBC Outdoor Club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Whistler, explore Vancouver Island, hike Grouse Grind, take weekend trips to the Rockies or Banff. Vancouver is a perfect base for travel and adventure.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. People were friendly and welcoming, and the culture felt both familiar and distinct from Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs early, participate in class, and attend campus events. Canadians are open but you need to take initiative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The academic competitiveness and focus on participation was a shift from my experience at UCPH. Also, tipping culture took some getting used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multiculturalism, respect for Indigenous communities, and the outdoor lifestyle were inspiring and refreshing

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply early for courses and housing – spots fill up fast.
2. Join at least one student club to meet people.
3. Take advantage of the stunning natural surroundings – pack for rain and outdoor activities!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan your travel around reading week and holidays. Buy a rain jacket – it rains a lot in Vancouver!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world and learning about Indigenous legal systems in a hands-on academic setting. Also getting to ski and hike the BEAUTIFUL nature surronding campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating the registration process and adjusting to the North American academic structure with its frequent assessments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: This exchange was one of the most enriching parts of my education. I highly recommend UBC and Vancouver to anyone who enjoys nature and is curious about different legal perspectives.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
